title.zh: 卷36 志十一 天文十一 五星合聚
title.en: Volume 36 Treatises 11: Astronomy 11, Conjunctions of the Five Planets

sentences.zh: 五星合聚

translations.literal: Conjunctions of the Five Planets.
translations.idiomatic: Conjunctions of the Five Planets

sentences.zh: 天官書言同舍為合，於兩星、三星、四星、五星之合各有占，而以五星合為最吉，謂經度之同如合朔也。

translations.literal: The Treatise on the Offices of Heaven says that sharing a lodge is called "conjunction"; conjunctions of two, three, four, and five stars each have their prognostications, but a conjunction of all five planets is most auspicious—meaning their ecliptic longitudes align as at a new moon.
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on the Offices of Heaven states that when stars share a lodge it counts as a conjunction; prognostications differ for pairings of two, three, four, or five stars, yet a full conjunction of the five planets is held most auspicious—namely when their ecliptic longitudes coincide as at new moon.

sentences.zh: 茲就三星以上同宮同宿，及兩星以上同度者，著於篇。

translations.literal: Here are recorded cases of three or more stars sharing a palace and lodge, and of two or more stars sharing a degree.
translations.idiomatic: This chapter records instances in which three or more stars shared a palace and lodge, and those in which two or more stars shared the same degree.
